requirement:
A plain-text outline has a root for the whole file and one anonymous `line`
child per nonblank line, in source order. Blank lines create no child nodes.
Each line's selector is `line@<identity-hash-prefix>` under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. The prefix derives from its
contents rather than its line number. Identical lines are interchangeable for
selection.
rationale:
The reviewed tests check every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.plain-text.items`. I did not read the implementation source. Expected behavior comes from the requirement text.

**Root for the whole file**
- `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors]` asserts the root has the empty selector `""` and spans `0..18`, the whole 18-byte source. It also checks that an empty file gives only a root with span `0..0`.
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` asserts the root span is `0..source.len()` and its selector is `""`.

**One anonymous `line` child per nonblank line, in source order, with no children for blank lines**
- `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` parses `"alpha\n\n  beta  \nalpha\n"` and expects exactly 3 line selectors.
- The `unknown_extensions…` test expects 4 items in total (the root plus 3 lines) and checks that the line spans slice out to `["alpha","beta","alpha"]`, which establishes source order.
- It also checks that every child has kind `line`.
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` covers a whitespace-only line (`" \t"`) and gives it no item. It also checks the byte spans `0..2` and `6..10` of the non-ASCII lines.

**Selector form `line@<identity-hash-prefix>`**
- The `unknown_extensions…` test strips the `line@` prefix. It asserts the prefix is 12 characters long, all hex digits, and equal to `structural_hash[..12]`.
- The `plain_text_lines…` test asserts that all selectors start with `line@`. It also asserts that a line node's `structural_hash` equals `hash::line("beta")`.

**Prefix derives from content, not line number**
- The `unknown_extensions…` test reflows the same lines onto different line numbers, with extra blank lines and different surrounding whitespace. The `alpha` selector stays the same.
- The same test asserts that `alpha` and `beta` get different selectors.
- The `plain_text_lines…` test asserts that `"two  words"` and `"two words"` give the same selector, while `"twowords"` gives a different one.

**Identical lines are interchangeable for selection**
- In the `plain_text_lines…` test, `selectors[0] == selectors[2]` and `outline.resolve(&selectors[0])` succeeds.
- In the `unknown_extensions…` test, `first.select(&alpha.selector)` returns the text `"alpha"`, and the first and third line selectors are equal.
- The unicode test selects each line by its selector and checks the text.

The cited `requirements.references.outline_selectors` is covered where this subject applies it. These cases are the `line@hash` form, the 12-hex-digit prefix, a `line` selector that resolves when any matching line exists, and no line numbers in selectors.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept. All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.

An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
